change.migration: 20261106120000_encode_attempt_isolation adds nullable VideoEncodeJob.attemptId and rejects a transition into RUNNING when attemptId is null; an already RUNNING legacy row can continue heartbeats.
change.claim: Every new claim assigns gen_random_uuid() in the same UPDATE that moves the row to RUNNING.
change.ownership: New attempt UUID is carried by the worker job, distinct local work directory, HLS asset/object prefixes, finalizer lookup, audit metadata, diagnostics and prefix cleanup. Legacy rows with null attemptId continue using the original version prefix until recovered.

postgres.command: DATABASE_URL=<disposable-local-PostgreSQL-17> DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED=<same> npx prisma migrate deploy && npx vitest run --config vitest.postgres.config.ts tests/postgres/encode-attempt-isolation.pg.test.ts --reporter=json
scenarios: Legacy claim without attemptId is rejected and the row remains QUEUED.
Two successive claims of one job receive distinct UUIDs and disjoint prefixes.
An already RUNNING legacy job can heartbeat; after stale recovery it is claimed with a fresh UUID and activeOriginalId is unchanged.
postgres.environment: Disposable postgres:17-alpine container removed after the run; all repository migrations applied.

limits: No controlled shutdown/drain was performed against a running environment. Documentation requires legacy workers to be drained before applying the migration and starting new workers.
No R2/S3 sandbox or independent review was available.
K17 is still required to fence activation, job status changes and cleanup side effects from a stale worker that resumes after takeover; K16 does not close R02.
